check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 warning).

1. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: Tube A1 in slot 3 never mixed after library 96 went in (1% of the
well)
   line 33:  p300.dispense(25, pool_tube)
   At line 33 the robot added library 96 to tube A1 in slot 3, which already held library 1,
   library 2, library 3, library 4 and 91 more. The addition was 1% of the well, nothing
   mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a
   small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration
   you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will
   mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix tube A1 in slot 3 after line 33: `mix_after=(5, 1920)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 1920, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [80df5f525de9]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: Tube A1 in slot 3 never mixed after library 96 went in (1% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 33 the robot added library 96 to tube A1 in slot 3, which already held library 1, library 2, library 3, library 4 and 91 more. The addition was 1% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix tube A1 in slot 3 after line 33: `mix_after=(5, 1920)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 1920, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
